Loading libraries

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)
```
## Problem 2

Loading, tidying, merging data:

```{r}
covar_df =
  read_csv("./data/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4) |>
  janitor::clean_names()

accel_df =
  read_csv("./data/nhanes_accel.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()

nhanes_df = inner_join(covar_df, accel_df, by = "seqn")

nhanes_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na(sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  mutate(
    seqn = as.character(seqn),
    sex = case_match(
      sex,
      1 ~ "male",
      2 ~ "female"),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("male", "female")),
    education = case_match(
      education,
      1 ~ "less than high school",
      2 ~ "high school equivalent",
      3 ~ "more than high school"),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c("less than high school",
                 "high school equivalent",
                 "more than high school")))

nhanes_df
```

Education and sex table:

```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Men and women are about evenly split in the "less than high school" group (27 men, 28 women) and the "more than high school" group (56 men, 59 women). In the "high school equivalent" group there are more men than women (35 vs. 23). The "more than high school" group is by far the largest, with 115 participants.

Plot:

```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = education, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Age distribution by sex and education",
    x = "Education",
    y = "Age (years)")
```

Total activity and age:

```{r}
nhanes_long_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims") |>
  mutate(minute = as.numeric(minute))

total_df =
  nhanes_long_df |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  summarize(total_activity = sum(mims))

total_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity vs. age",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily MIMS") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Total activity generally decreases with age for both sexes in all three education groups. The decline is steepest in the "less than high school" group. The decline is weakest in the "more than high school" group.

24 hour activity, 3 panel plot:

```{r}
nhanes_long_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = seqn), alpha = .05) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = sex), se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "24-hour activity by education and sex",
    x = "Minute of the day",
    y = "MIMS") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

All three education groups follow the same daily pattern. Activity is very low overnight, rises sharply in the early morning, stays high through the daytime, and drops off in the evening. 

## Problem 3

Importing and tidying data

```{r}
jan_2020_df =
  read_csv("./data/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(year = "2020", month = "January")

july_2020_df =
  read_csv("./data/July 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(year = "2020", month = "July")

jan_2024_df =
  read_csv("./data/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(year = "2024", month = "January")

july_2024_df =
  read_csv("./data/July 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(year = "2024", month = "July")

citi_df =
  bind_rows(jan_2020_df, july_2020_df, jan_2024_df, july_2024_df) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July")),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
                 "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")),
    rideable_type = factor(rideable_type),
    member_casual = factor(member_casual, levels = c("member", "casual"))) |>
  select(ride_id, year, month, weekdays, everything())

citi_df
```

The cleaned dataset contains `r nrow(citi_df)` rides from four months (January and July of 2020 and 2024). Each ride has its year and month (added from the file names), the day of the week, ride duration in minutes, bike type (classic or electric), rider type (member or casual), and the names of the start and end stations. Duration ranges from 1 minute to about 239 minutes.


Total number of rides in each combination of year and month:

```{r}
citi_df |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n) |>
  mutate(total = member + casual) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Rides are more common in July than in January in both years and there are more rides in 2024 than in 2020 in both months. The sample contains 12,420 rides in January 2020 and 18,861 in January 2024. For July, it contains 21,048 rides in 2020 and 47,156 in 2024. 

Most popular starting stations in July 2024:

```{r}
citi_df |>
  filter(year == "2024", month == "July") |>
  drop_na(start_station_name) |>
  count(start_station_name, name = "n_rides") |>
  arrange(desc(n_rides)) |>
  head(5) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The five most popular starting stations in July 2024 are Pier 61 at Chelsea Piers, University Pl & E 14 St, W 21 St & 6 Ave, West St & Chambers St and W 31 St & 7 Ave. 

Median ride duration by day of week, month, year:

```{r}
citi_df |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(median_duration = median(duration)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekdays, y = median_duration, color = month, group = month)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(. ~ year) +
  labs(
    title = "Median ride duration by day of week, month, and year",
    x = "Day of the week",
    y = "Median duration (minutes)",
    color = "Month") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Median ride duration is longer in July than in January in both years. The seasonal difference is much larger in 2020 (medians of about 8.9 minutes in January vs. 14.6 in July) than in 2024 (about 7.7 vs. 9.6). Rides are longer on weekends than on weekdays in most cases.

Ride duration in 2024 by month, rider type, bike type:

```{r}
citi_df |>
  filter(year == "2024") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = duration, fill = rideable_type)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ member_casual) +
  labs(
    title = "Ride duration in 2024 by month, rider type, and bike type",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Duration (minutes)",
    fill = "Bike type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

In 2024, casual riders take longer rides than members in every combination of month and bike type. Rides are longer in July than in January for both groups. Among casual riders, electric bike rides are shorter than classic bike rides (about 9 vs. 13 minutes in January, and 13 vs. 16 minutes in July). Among members, the two bike types are more similar, with electric bike rides slightly longer in July (about 9.2 vs. 7.7 minutes).
